Literally the most generic storyline a videogame could come up with. You knew the ending of the damn game within the first hour of gameplay.

There are multiple campaigns. Which do you speak of?

If it's the Dragon, you're supposed to know and that's the point. You aren't living your character, you're living his story. You know you kill the dragon just like you knew Beowulf was going to slay the Dragon from the first chapter. It's the journey, not the destination, that made the story. Thus, the story is as deep as your want it. You could slay the other Dragonborn in Morrowind, or you could avoid him. Your exploits of bandit camps, vampire dens and Orc Strongholds, makes you who you are just as well as your factions, political beliefs, and preferred God. The only reason Skyrim would be "generic" to you is if you didn't even play it or only played the main storyline, and that's not the point of the TES games.

And no, it's not the most generic storyline a videogame could come up with. The interpretation of mythical creatures is almost entirely unique. In Skyrim, dragons are simple, greedy, brutish flying creatures that have invaded en masse by raising from the dead. That is a sentence I would not use to describe any other game. Tamriel's lore, in and out of Skyrim, is so deep and rich that there are communities devoted to it, (on reddit, so I won't link) so don't pull the "it's generic" excuse on me.

Sure, it was overhyped. People called Skyrim the best game ever played when it came out, and I disagree. That doesn't mean it isn't a fantastic game.
